rules.label: Cable runs are recorded separately from cores
rules.guidance: A cable line may state a number of parallel runs as well as a core count. Notation such as 2R x 4C x 25 sqmm means two runs of four-core 25 sqmm cable - record 2 as runs and 4 as core. Runs and cores are separate values for cables and must never be multiplied together: the core count identifies which cable in the catalog, and the run count multiplies its price. If a run count is not stated anywhere in the context supplied for the row, record 1. If a core count is not stated, record 1.

rules.label: Conduit named on a wiring or cabling line
rules.guidance: A wiring or cabling line often describes the conduit the cable runs in. Report only what the document says and never infer a value it does not give. conduit_included: answer Yes when the document says this line supplies the conduit or carries its cost, for example 'drawn through 20mm MS conduit', 'cost to be inclusive of conduit', 'the scope shall include Wires, Conduit, Bends'. Answer No when the document says the conduit already exists or is somebody else's scope, for example 'in existing conduit', 'laid in already laid GI conduit', 'the supply and installation of conduit is part of the electrical contractor'. Answer Unclear when a conduit is named but the document does not say who carries its cost. Leave it unstated when the line names no conduit at all. conduit_type: the conduit material the document names - PVC, MS or GI. size_mm: the conduit diameter in millimetres the document states. Leave either unstated when the document does not give it.

rules.label: Whether a pop-up box includes its modules
rules.guidance:
A pop-up or floor box line is priced one of two ways, and the first thing to decide is
which.

Read the line as INCLUDING modules only when it actually supplies them - when it
enumerates sockets, switches, chargers or outlets that sit in the box, or says the box is
supplied populated, loaded, fitted or complete with them. Set Includes modules to Yes and
fill in the module attributes for what it names.

Read the line as WITHOUT modules when it supplies the box alone - the enclosure, the
lid, the frame, the mounting arrangement - with nothing named inside it. Set Includes
modules to No and return None for every module attribute: the switch, all four sockets,
the blank plate and the face plate. Colour is not a module attribute: leave it to its
default unless the row names one.

Language that anticipates modules is not the same as supplying them. A box described as
having provision to take, being suitable for, shall support, can accommodate, or is
designed for a number of modules is a box WITHOUT modules - it states a capacity, not
contents. So is a line that explicitly excludes them, such as modules to be supplied
separately, box to exclude the modules, or modules by others. In every one of those cases
answer No.

A module count on its own is a capacity too. A twelve module pop-up box is a twelve
module enclosure; it does not tell you that twelve modules are being supplied.

When the line does include modules but names something the catalog does not carry, fill
in the parts you can read and leave the rest blank rather than forcing a wrong match.

Leave Includes modules blank only when the line genuinely does not say either way.

rules.label: Industrial socket paired MCB
rules.guidance: Industrial socket lines are often billed together with the MCB that controls them. Report what the line SAYS about that MCB; the pairing itself is computed downstream. (0) `paired_mcb`: ALWAYS return null for this attribute, even when the text names a specific MCB - the pairing is computed downstream from the facts you report. (1) `mcb_present`: "Yes" only when the text itself NAMES a breaker. The row's `description`, its `notes`, or an `ancestor_chain` entry must contain the word MCB - or an unambiguous equivalent: MCCB, RCBO, RCCB, ELCB, "miniature circuit breaker", "circuit breaker". A word must actually be present: this is a reading test, not a judgement. The following are NOT mentions, and each of them on its own means "No": an incomer or incoming supply; any current or amperage figure, including the socket's own rating; a distribution board, trolley, panel or feeder context; internal wiring; protection implied by the kind of equipment described. When no such word appears, answer "No". If you are unsure, answer "No" - a socket priced without an MCB is corrected in one click, a socket priced with an MCB nobody asked for is invisible. (2) `mcb_amp_a`: if the text states a current specifically for the MCB, use it; otherwise the HIGHEST current stated anywhere in the text (a socket's stated current serves the MCB when no separate MCB current is given). '25/20/16 A' gives 25. Read it from the text itself, never from the `rating` attribute, whose values are ranges that lose the individual figures. Leave it blank only when the text states no current at all. (3) `mcb_pole_stated`: the pole DESIGNATION the text uses for the MCB, recorded VERBATIM as one of the allowed values - do not convert it. 'TPN', 'TP+N', 'TP+NL', 'TP+2N' and 'TP+2NL' each mean four pole and must be recorded exactly as the text writes them, never shortened to 'TP' and never to a shorter one of each other; the conversion to the catalogue's pole is computed downstream from what you report. Leave it "None" when the text does not state one; do not infer it from the socket's pin count. (4) `mcb_curve_stated`: the curve the text states (C or D). Leave it "None" when none is stated. Steps (2), (3) and (4) describe the MCB only when `mcb_present` is "Yes". When you answered "No", return `mcb_amp_a` blank and `mcb_pole_stated` / `mcb_curve_stated` as "None" - there is no MCB to describe, so there is nothing to read. Deciding (1) is not a consequence of being able to answer (2): a current figure in the text is never evidence that an MCB exists.

rules.label: A stated 6A switch is priced as 10A

rules.label: Switch way count defaults to 1 way

Catalog switch items name their way count - 1 WAY or 2 WAY. When the context

rules.label: The back box's own module count
rules.guidance: box_modules_stated is the module size of the BACK BOX itself, as a count of modules. The count may sit anywhere in the row's payload: the row's own text, its notes, or any entry of its ancestor_chain, nearest entry first. Write the count exactly as the text writes it, without converting it to anything else; where the text writes more than one count for the box, write every one of them as written. Leave it null when no module count for the box appears anywhere in the payload: a size given only in millimetres is not a module count, and a count of ports, nodes or outlets is not one either, so never derive it from those. This attribute describes only the box; it changes nothing about how any other attribute is read.

rules.label: Shell size: exact or next higher
rules.guidance: When selecting the DB shell, match the stated way-count to the catalog exactly. If the exact way-count is not in the catalog, select the NEXT HIGHER way-count, never a lower one. A stated range takes the highest value first.

rules.label: RCCB/RCBO with no stated current: highest available mA
rules.guidance: When a BoQ line describes an RCCB or RCBO but NO leakage current rating is stated anywhere in the context supplied for that row - not in its own description or notes, and not in any ancestor context provided - match the catalog on the other parameters that ARE stated: device type, amp rating, pole configuration. Among the items that match, select the one with the HIGHEST mA rating. If the catalog cannot be matched on those other parameters, leave it BLANK - do not substitute a different amp rating, pole configuration or device type to force a match. When a current IS stated anywhere in the supplied context, match that stated value as normal.

rules.label: ELCB priced as MCB + RCCB
rules.guidance: An ELCB is a combined device and is priced as TWO components: an MCB plus an RCCB. When a BoQ line describes an ELCB, fill two slots - one MCB and one RCCB - both at the stated amp rating and pole configuration. If the ELCB line states a leakage current, apply it to the RCCB; if it states none, R3 applies to the RCCB.

rules.label: Outgoings stated per phase multiply by phase count
rules.guidance: When a BoQ line states a quantity of outgoings or sub-outgoings PER PHASE, the quantity to record is the total across all phases, not the per-phase figure. Multiply the stated per-phase quantity by the number of phases the DB carries: three for a TPN or VTPN DB, one for an SPN DB. For example, a TPN DB described as having 10 Nos of 6A MCB per phase carries 30 in total; the same wording on an SPN DB carries 10. The phase type may be stated anywhere in the context supplied for the row, including in the DB or shell description. Record the multiplied total as the quantity for that slot.

steps.explain: PIECE 4: a row naming ONLY a primary/first point takes the Pricing Input 'Point wiring - circuit length of the first point'; ONLY a secondary/looping/second/third point takes 'Point wiring - circuit length per further point'. Both types, neither, or confusion -> on_miss skip leaves the formula's value standing, unchanged. Placed AFTER derive_attribute so the substitution marks '(computed)'. *** ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: this step runs BEFORE derive_attribute, not after. prefer_attr reads the SAME attribute, so after derive it would read the value derive just computed, call it stated, and the first-point / further-point substitution could NEVER fire. Before derive it sees only what the ROW stated: a stated length is kept (plain), otherwise the input's length is written (computed), and derive then keeps whichever landed. A row stating nothing and naming no type falls through both and gets the formula. *** *** prefer_attr IS LOAD-BEARING (owner ruling 2026-09-01, after the cert caught it): a STATED length SURVIVES this substitution, and the two inputs apply ONLY where the row states none. Without it the map overwrites a number the document wrote down -- BOQ-26-00141 r130 reads 'Upto 6 Meters' and would have priced the first-point length instead, over-quoting wire and conduit per point. It also honours the older owner-locked rule on the derive step above: a STATED length is kept exactly as given. The more specific reading wins; the inference is the fallback. *** ELR-3a: the two lengths are Pricing Inputs (table_from_ctx), read by the rate_ref steps appended below.

circuit length = the Pricing Input 'Point wiring - circuit length of the first point' for one point, + 'Point wiring - circuit length per further point' for every additional point; a STATED length is kept exactly as given (no floor, no warning)

the run itself: handed off to a raceway/tray/existing conduit -> no conduit bought. 'Either' is the slash alternation and INCLUDES (owner: genuinely ambiguous). DEFAULT Yes = silence INCLUDES -- the OPPOSITE of wiring_cabling's default No, deliberately
a NORMAL conduit named elsewhere makes the row ambiguous -> INCLUDE (owner ruling). Flexible/None leave the previous verdict untouched -- the flexible piece is the drop at the fixture, not the run
an EXPLICIT exclusion in the document outranks every inference above it -- placed LAST so it wins

PIECE 3: a STATED material stays plain; silence takes PVC and renders '(computed)'. prefer_attr is the attribute ITSELF (the panel-visible rule) and the default is LOAD-BEARING -- without it a silent row is narrowed out of the missing-gate exemption and prices NOTHING, which is what the 161 silent rows did before this slice

the DROP, applied AFTER the default so it is not undone by it: conduit_included No -> the 'None' sentinel, which circuit_fit's absent_when reads as POSITIVE ABSENCE and the conduit component's none_skips zeroes. Renders 'None (computed)'

THE CIRCUIT STRETCH, the Pricing Input 'Point wiring - circuit wiring stretch, DB to the first point' (owner ruling), ONCE per row. prefer_attr is the attribute ITSELF (the panel-display rule), so a pricer's edit is kept and renders PLAIN while the input's value renders '(computed)'. The table's 0 is the field-1=No shape and is LOAD-BEARING: a BLANK length would make resolveQty return null and refuse the whole pipeline, where 0 is an honest quantity. *** result_attr is circuit_wire_length_m, NEVER circuit_length_m -- that one holds the POINT stretch (the first-point / further-point lengths) and a typo here would silently retarget it. ***
the EFFECTIVE circuit quantity starts as the length above. Hidden (panel:false) because the next step writes the owner's exclusion into it, which is a CODE decision and not a field a pricer edits.

THE SECONDARY EXCLUSION (owner: 'the ciricuit wiring cost wil be added only to thr eprimary point rows or mixed rows and not secondary point rows'). It reuses the SHIPPED point_type verdict (extraction.point_type_of) -- there is no second reader. on_miss skip means Primary, mixed and SILENT rows all keep the full stretch; only a row the matcher reads as Secondary is zeroed. *** It lands on circuit_qty_m, NOT on the visible length field: a Secondary row still SHOWS 30 m, because the owner's field shape puts 0 on the length only when circuit wiring is absent. ***
overall dia = sum sqrt(sqmm/pi)*2*cores*runs; smallest conduit whose usable dia fits; circuits = ROUNDDOWN(usable/dia); conduit qty = ROUNDUP(length/circuits)

modules = the weighted sum of the stated quantities; the plate priced is the LARGER of the stated and the computed count (a stated plate is a FLOOR, never a ceiling, and an upgrade is named in the trace); the back box takes the SELECTED plate's module COUNT re-fit on its own (shorter) ladder, or the computed count when there is no plate

Multiplier provenance: wires K4 0.602 / M4 0.4515 / install x(1+I6=1.0); conduit H3 0.7 / I3 0.5 / F4 0.2; switches L 0.3625 / M 0.25 / J7 0.2 (uniform across families, verified 2026-07-30). | EA-4a-r (2026-07-31): None mechanism. socket/switch/plate/wire2 are allow_none; selecting None disables the dependent inputs (qty; wire2 core; plate None ALSO disables back_box since the box is keyed by plate size) and the line contributes ZERO; circuit_fit omits wire2 from the dia when wire2=None (single-wire point). None = positive absence (distinct from blank=unknown); extraction returns None when an enumerated bill names no such component, blank when the row is vague. | PW-CONDUIT-OPTIONAL + LENGTH-BY-POINT-TYPE (v50): the conduit is now droppable and the circuit length can be substituted. THE CONDUIT DECISION IS CODE, NEVER THE MODEL: the model reports three facts (conduit_handoff / other_conduit / conduit_price_excluded, all panel:false) and a three-step map_attribute chain applies the owner's decision table. DROP happens on exactly three shapes - an explicit price exclusion; a handed-off run with no other conduit; a handed-off run whose only other conduit is FLEXIBLE. EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDES PVC, including the slash alternation and silence. *** OPPOSITE DEFAULTS, BY DESIGN: wiring_cabling (F-28) maps conduit_included default 'No' - a CABLE row silent on conduit EXCLUDES it. point_wiring maps default 'Yes' - a POINT WIRING row silent on conduit INCLUDES PVC. Point wiring normally carries conduit; cables normally do not. DO NOT HARMONISE THEM: a future editor who makes them agree breaks one. *** ERROR DIRECTION: a wrong reading here UNDER-quotes, silently, and nothing on screen says a component was skipped - the mirror of the cable case, where a wrong reading over-quoted and a human noticed. That is why every ambiguous shape includes. circuit_length_m: point_type Primary -> the Pricing Input 'Point wiring - circuit length of the first point', Secondary -> the Pricing Input 'Point wiring - circuit length per further point', anything else leaves the formula standing: 'Point wiring - circuit length of the first point' + (points - 1) x 'Point wiring - circuit length per further point'. A STATED length WINS over all of it (owner 2026-09-01): the map carries prefer_attr, so those two Pricing Inputs fire only where the row states no length. | PW-CIRCUIT-STRETCH (v51): a point wiring row whose text POSITIVELY includes the circuit (submain) run from the DB now carries that wire too. EIGHT new panel fields (circuit_wire_included, circuit wire 1 and 2 core/runs/thickness, circuit_wire_length_m) plus the hidden circuit_qty_m. *** ONE RATE, TWO PARTS: the circuit amount is a COMPONENT of the point rate, added flat, ONCE per row, never multiplied or divided by the point count. The two pw_circuit_* pipelines exist ONLY to give it its own labelled block (the termination_boq precedent); their outputs name no rate kind, so they can never feed the applied value and the collapsed headline stays the single point rate. *** THE SECONDARY EXCLUSION IS CODE: the shipped point_type verdict zeroes circuit_qty_m on a Secondary row; Primary, mixed and SILENT rows are charged. *** THE TWO CIRCUIT THICKNESSES CARRY allow_none AND NO DEFAULT, and the extraction_none_guidance above is what makes that safe: "None" means the document says there is no such wire (price nothing, quietly and correctly); BLANK means the model could not read the gauge (the row REFUSES and a pricer supplies it). Conflating them turns the owner's ruled LOUD failure into a silent under-quote. *** circuit_length_m IS UNTOUCHED -- it holds the POINT stretch ('Point wiring - circuit length of the first point' / 'Point wiring - circuit length per further point' by point type) and is merely misnamed; do not rename it and never target it from a circuit step. | SLICE A (v52). F2: R12's WORKED EXAMPLE WAS A FALSE FRIEND, AND ITS REPLACEMENT QUOTES NOTHING. The retired example read "'recessed/surface existing conduit' ... so the answer there is Yes", and rows reading a mounting slash followed by a plain conduit description matched that SURFACE FORM while lacking the load-bearing word -- so conduit_handoff came back Yes and 36 rows silently dropped a conduit they supply. Measured unstable, not merely wrong: BOQ-26-00086 r51 and r53 share a word-for-word identical grandparent and near-identical text, and one priced its conduit while the other dropped it, both at 0.6 confidence. *** ATTEMPT 1 REPLACED IT WITH A CONTRASTING PAIR OF QUOTED PHRASES AND THAT BROKE A DIFFERENT RULE: the negative half quoted a string that also lives on rows whose chain says 'and circuit wiring with 2 x 2.5 sq mm', and R13's circuit-inclusion verdict flipped Yes -> No on them. Four config-switched runs: v51 Yes, v52 No, v52 No, v51 Yes. *** THE STRUCTURAL REASON, AND THE STANDING LESSON: every `rules` entry is injected into ONE ESTIMATOR_RULES block, so a rule cannot be edited in isolation -- a phrase quoted in one rule is visible to every other question the payload asks. ATTEMPT 2 THEREFORE STATES THE TEST AND QUOTES NO CORPUS TEXT AT ALL, and the mint asserts mechanically that it contains no such phrase. The decision table and the closing clause are UNCHANGED. *** F5: the four circuit CORE/RUNS fields lose `allow_none`. A None on runs never had a pricing effect -- `none_skips` reads only the component's ref bindings (core, thickness), and runs feeds `absentMeansOne`, which maps "None" to 1 -- so the checkbox promised a drop it could not deliver. Removal is MEASURED INERT: the REAL shipped helper prices 190 / refuses 61 over the 251 run-covered rows both with the flags and without, on the identical row set with identical blank tallies, because `disables_when_none` on the THICKNESS already greys and clears that wire's core and runs. *** BOTH THICKNESSES KEEP allow_none AND NO DEFAULT -- thickness is the working drop control and the loud-failure ruling depends on it. | SLICE B (v53). F1: R9 IS NOW A CONDUCTOR FLOOR. The invariant is `core x runs` SUMMED ACROSS THE WIRES THAT EXIST, raised UP to three and NEVER reduced. *** THE RULE WAS REVISED BY MEASUREMENT: the first formulation coerced RUNS, and on the 31 corpus rows reading `3 core, 1 run` that would have bought NINE conductors (+Rs 133,792, individual rows up to +194%), while on 5 rows the document states as three-phase it would have HALVED the copper (-Rs 27,535). Measured on conductors the corpus was ALREADY 231 of 237 compliant, and the other 6 sit ABOVE three -- which is why the rule is a floor. *** WHERE THE MISSING CONDUCTOR GOES (owner, 2026-09-03): a SINGLE-CORE short wire takes MORE RUNS and NO second wire is created; with two single-core wires the BIGGER one is raised; a MULTI-CORE short wire keeps its cores and gains a second wire of ONE core at the SAME size. *** "unless the line explicitly states otherwise" STAYS -- the instruction to delete it was withdrawn when the rule became a floor, because a stated count at or above three now always wins. *** THE INSTALL STEPPING IS CLOSED BY RULING, NOT OPEN: `mult_step_divisor: 3` exists on BOTH axes and is byte-identical, but it is applied PER COMPONENT and never summed across the pair, so two wires carrying three runs between them buy TWO install units. The owner ruled that CORRECT ("we are pricing the 2 wires separately") and ruled the 98 rows that would fall under summed stepping (76 point, 22 circuit) "ignore". Do NOT build multi-attribute stepping. *** F4a: the display-only pipelines pw_circuit_supply / pw_circuit_install are REMOVED with their labels -- the circuit money was always INSIDE the point rate and a second block read as an extra charge. *** F4b: the eight circuit fields carry `group_label`, a NEW GENERAL capability -- any attribute definition in any category may declare one and the panel emits a header when it CHANGES; a category declaring none is unaffected. It sits on the DEFINITION because top-level config keys are allowlisted while definition keys are documented as not, so it ships with no backend change. | SLICE B v4 (v54). THE CONDUCTOR FLOOR LEFT THE PROMPT AND BECAME CODE, and that is a CORRECTION rather than a new idea: the standing rule on this project is that the MODEL READS FACTS while every substitution, ladder and conversion lives in deterministic code or config. The floor is a SUBSTITUTION and was written as prose in R9, which it never should have been. *** THE COST, MEASURED TWICE IN TWO DAYS: every `rules` entry is injected into ONE ESTIMATOR_RULES block, so rewriting R12's conduit example flipped R13's circuit verdict on two rows, and extending R9's floor to NAME the circuit wires -- the only way prose could reach them -- moved R13's `circuit_wire_included` on BOQ-26-00200 r11 (Yes/Yes/No across three runs). *** SO R9 NOW ONLY TEACHES READING and is POINT-SCOPED; it names no circuit wire, states no total, and the phrase "unless the line explicitly states otherwise" is REMOVED because it excepted a total R9 no longer states. The enforcement is `extraction.apply_conductor_floor`, declared here by a `conductor_floor` block on each of the four THICKNESS definitions (the wire existence markers) -- config-driven, naming no category, and inert for every config declaring none. *** PROVEN SAFE BEFORE THE PROSE WAS TOUCHED: the corrector was run over all 237 in-axis POINT rows of the live corpus and changed ZERO of them, byte-identical to what the prose produced. *** THE RULE: conductors = core x runs summed over the wires that EXIST (a "None" thickness means the wire does not exist and contributes nothing, whatever its mirrored default runs say); a FLOOR of three, never a cap, nothing ever reduced; a single-core short wire takes MORE RUNS and no second wire; the BIGGER of two single-core wires is raised; a multi-core short wire gains a second ONE-core wire at the SAME thickness.
point_wiring.extraction_none_guidance:
return "None" when the row's enumerated bill names NO such component (positive absence -- a real light point may have a switch and plate but no socket, or a single wire and no second wire); return null/blank ONLY when the row is too vague to tell.

THE TWO ANSWERS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND THE CIRCUIT WIRE THICKNESSES ARE WHERE IT MATTERS MOST. On circuit_wire1_thickness_sqmm and circuit_wire2_thickness_sqmm: answer "None" ONLY when the document positively indicates there is no such circuit wire -- it carries no circuit or submain wiring at all, or it names one circuit wire and no second one. If the row DOES carry circuit wiring but you cannot tell what gauge it is, answer NOTHING: leave it blank/null. NEVER answer "None" to mean "I could not read it". The two answers have opposite consequences: a BLANK stops the row and a pricer is asked to supply the size, whereas "None" prices the row with no circuit wire at all and nobody is asked.

rules.label: Wire runs, cores, and the number of points in point wiring
rules.guidance:
Report the wire specification EXACTLY AS THE LINE STATES IT. Do not add,
complete or balance anything: if the line gives one wire, report one wire; if
it gives a run count, report that count, whatever it is.

Read the line as follows.

When a run count is stated, such as 3R x 1.5 sqmm, record it as given: 3 runs,
1 core.

When a size is given with a plain multiplier and no run marker, such as
3 x 1.5 sqmm, the multiplier is the run count: 3 runs, 1 core, 1.5 sqmm.

When only a size is given with no multiplier at all, such as 1.5 sqmm, record
1 run of 1 core at that size -- the line states no count, so do not invent one.

In each of those cases, look for a second conductor named separately - an
earth wire, or any further size - before deciding there is only one wire. A
separately named earth wire IS a second wire: record the first size as wire 1
with the runs the line gives it, and the named earth as wire 2 with its own.

When the line states two different run counts, such as two runs of 2.5 sqmm
and one run of 1.5 sqmm, record the wire with the higher run count as wire 1
and the lower as wire 2.

When the line gives two sizes with no run counts at all, record the larger
size as wire 1 and the smaller as wire 2, ONE run each -- the line states no
counts, so do not invent them. Which is larger still decides the order.

Record a core count greater than 1 only when the line positively states
multiple cores - 2C, two core, 3 core. A number before the size is a run
count, not a core count.

Also record the NUMBER OF POINTS the line covers. A line reading Set of seven
(7) light points covers 7; Three (3) light point covers 3; a line describing a
single outlet or a single socket on a breaker covers 1. Where the line names
no count at all, record 1. Count the points the line prices, not the number of
such lines in the bill.

rules.label: More than one socket means a 16A switch
rules.guidance:
When a row carries more than one socket, price the switch as 16A regardless
   of the rating stated in the BoQ. This overrides any other rule about switch
   amp rating, including the substitution of a stated 6A switch.

rules.label: A stated 6A switch is priced as 10A
rules.guidance:
No 6A switch exists in the catalog. When a line states a 6A switch, select
   the 10A switch with the same other parameters - the same way count, the same
   indicator option, the same colour. If no 10A variant matches those other
   parameters, leave it blank rather than substituting a different way count or
   indicator option.

rules.label: Switch way count defaults to 1 way
rules.guidance:
Catalog switch items name their way count - 1 WAY or 2 WAY. When the context
   supplied for a row does not state whether a switch is one way or two way,
   select the 1 WAY variant. When the text does state it, match what it says.

rules.label: What the row says about conduit
rules.guidance:
A point wiring line often says what the wiring runs through. Report only what the document says and never infer a value it does not give. Never decide whether the conduit should be priced - that decision is made elsewhere from your answers.

conduit_handoff: answer Yes when the document says this run uses something already there - a raceway, a cable tray, trunking, or an existing conduit. Answer Either ONLY when the document offers a choice between two DIFFERENT CONTAINERS - a conduit versus a raceway, a tray, or trunking - for example 'in existing conduit / raceway'. A slash between anything else is NOT a choice of container and must NOT be read as Either. Such a slash almost always describes how the conduit is MOUNTED, and how a conduit is mounted says nothing about who supplies it.
Decide this field by ONE TEST: does the document say the conduit is ALREADY THERE? Only words to that effect -- that it is existing, already laid, already provided, previously installed, or supplied under another item -- make it already there. If such a word is present, answer Yes. If the line merely DESCRIBES a conduit -- how it is mounted, its gauge, material, size, grade or make -- and nothing anywhere says it is already there, then this line supplies that conduit and the answer is No. The same test applies to a slash between sizes, materials, grades or makes.
This field is ONLY about who supplies the conduit. It is not about the wiring, and nothing you decide here should change any other answer. Answer No when the run uses a conduit this line supplies. Leave it unstated when the line says nothing about what the wiring runs through.

other_conduit: answer Flexible when the only other conduit the line names is a flexible one, for example a flexible conduit at the drop of a light fixture. Answer Normal when it names an ordinary rigid conduit somewhere other than the run itself. Answer None when it names no other conduit. Leave it unstated when you cannot tell.

conduit_price_excluded: answer Yes ONLY when the document plainly says the conduit's price is not in this rate - for example 'conduit shall be paid under separate line item', 'the cost should be exclusive of conduits', 'conduit by others'. Answer No when it says the conduit cost IS included. Leave it unstated when the document does not address the conduit's price. Beware the opposite polarity: 'cost of conduit is included' is NOT an exclusion.

rules.label: Whether the rate includes the circuit wiring, and what that circuit wire is
rules.applies_to: circuit_wire_included, circuit_wire1_core, circuit_wire1_runs, circuit_wire1_thickness_sqmm, circuit_wire2_core, circuit_wire2_runs, circuit_wire2_thickness_sqmm
rules.guidance:
Some point wiring lines also cover the CIRCUIT (submain) wiring that feeds the point -- the run from the distribution board to the switch board or to the first point. That is a different conductor from the point wiring itself, and it is priced separately. Report only what the document says and never infer a value it does not give. Never decide whether the circuit wiring should be charged -- that decision is made elsewhere from your answers.

circuit_wire_included: answer Yes ONLY when the line POSITIVELY says its rate covers that run -- for example 'including circuit wiring from the DB', 'the rate shall include wiring from the distribution board to the switch board', 'inclusive of circuit main'. A heading that merely DESCRIBES the point wiring, even one naming a distribution board and a wire size, is NOT such a statement: 'Primary Light / Fan Point Circuit Wiring Controlled from DB with 2.5 sqmm x 3 Wire' describes what the point wiring IS, and the answer there is No. Answer No when the line says nothing about a separate circuit run, and No when it puts that run outside this rate ('circuit wiring paid under a separate item', 'excluding circuit main'). SILENCE IS No: the line must carry positive inclusion language.

circuit_wire1_core / circuit_wire1_runs / circuit_wire1_thickness_sqmm and the wire 2 equivalents: these describe the CIRCUIT wire, not the point wire. Read them from whatever the line says about the run from the distribution board, using the same reading conventions R9 gives for the point wiring. Where the line names circuit wiring but gives no size for it, leave the thickness BLANK -- never "None".

electrical_pricing_inputs.notes: The numbers our pricing rules read: a discount, a markup, a wastage, a BCS ratio, an installation share or a flat amount. The BCS and BoQ multipliers are DERIVED from these and are never stored. No pipelines and no attribute definitions, so this category can never price a BoQ row.

attribute_definitions.label: Item family
attribute_definitions.note: What the item IS. 'grille, type not stated' when the text gives a grille but not its type; 'none of these' for a priceable thing outside the sheet's families (owner ruling 6b: no SKU in the catalogue means the row is left blank for the user to decide). A discrete grille is 'grille, type not stated'. A row that gives only a size, or a size and a place ('600x600 for hub room'), buys the item its heading or that heading's note describes: answer that family, never 'none of these' with the size as its name. A row that buys something returns at least one item: an item outside the list is 'none of these' with 'Item as written' -- never an empty list. ALTERNATIVE NAMES (owner ruling 3a, 2026-09-23): a single skin plenum, a spill air box / spill air plenum, a plenum box, a diffuser box or a mixing chamber is 'mixing box / LP plenum'; 'double-skin plenum' ONLY when the text says double skin / double-skinned. Every louvre (intake, exhaust, discharge, fresh air, non-vision) is 'intake louvre'; a non-vision door louver is 'door grille'; a tegular or plaque diffuser is 'square diffuser'; on a row priced per sq.m, a diffuser whose shape the row and its headings do not settle -- no shape named, or round and square both offered ('round/square') -- is 'square diffuser' (owner 2026-10-23); a spigot damper is 'spigot' (code prices it as the Butterfly Damper With Spigot); a multi-blade louver damper is 'VCD'; a double deflection grille is 'linear grille' (a curved grille stays 'curved grille'); a grille damper is 'collar damper'; a floor tile grille, a rigid floor grille or a rigid tile grille is 'floor grille'. A Z-piece, a Z type baffle, a Z baffle or a cross talk silencer is 'cross-talk' (owner 2026-10-23), also under a heading that names another family (a Z type baffle under an ACTUATORS heading is 'cross-talk'). A return air baffle is 'cross-talk' (owner 2026-10-23); return it alone -- code adds its return air grille. A SECOND ITEM NEEDS WORDS: where nothing in the row or its own ancestors mentions a plenum box, a spill air box or a mixing chamber, a diffuser row pays for the diffuser alone -- do not add a box because diffusers often have one. Where an ancestor does describe the row's item as including one, both items are returned. A PLENUM'S ACCESSORIES ARE PART OF IT (owner 2026-10-23): where the row's item is a 'double-skin plenum' or a 'mixing box / LP plenum' itself, an access door or any other accessory the row names with it (hangers, cut-outs, openings) is not a second item -- return the plenum alone; its rate includes them. A canvas connection is NOT an accessory: where the row says its price includes canvas connections, return 'canvas connection' as a second item beside the plenum (owner 2026-10-23). A DAMPER NAMED AS PART OF A GRILLE OR DIFFUSER IS NOT A SECOND ITEM: a row buying a grille or a diffuser that the text says comes with a collar, volume-control or hit-and-miss damper pays for ONE item -- the grille or diffuser, with its damper attribute set. A damper is its own item only where the row buys the damper itself and names no host. A MOTORISED VCD'S CONTROL PANEL, ACTUATOR AND CABLING named in its heading are not separate items (owner 2026-10-23): return the VCD alone; code says on the panel that they are not included.

attribute_definitions.label: Damper
attribute_definitions.note: Owner default (R1) when 'None': without (curved grille: with). 'None' = the text says nothing about a damper. The ROW WINS over a heading: a row saying it is without a volume control damper is 'without', even where a neighbouring section heading names a damper product. WHERE THE ROW NAMES A DAMPER AS PART OF A GRILLE OR DIFFUSER, that is this item's damper: answer 'with' here and return no separate damper item. Three shapes this covers: a grille described with a collar damper; a curved or linear grille with its damper in the same sentence; a diffuser whose stated size is followed by a damper. Where the row buys dampers alone, the damper IS the item and this attribute describes nothing else.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulated
attribute_definitions.note: Owner default (R5, flexible duct) when 'None': insulated.

attribute_definitions.label: Air stream
attribute_definitions.note: Owner ruling 3c (2026-09-23): only when the row or its ancestors STATE it; otherwise 'None'. Never inferred from the kind of item.

attribute_definitions.label: Neck size (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: A SQUARE or rectangular item's neck size, as written. A round item's neck is its diameter and belongs in the diameter attribute instead.

attribute_definitions.label: Size (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: The item's OWN size, copied exactly as the row writes it, in ONE field: a face or outer size ("600 x 600"), or a box size with its depth ("525 x 525 x 450 mm"), or a single dimension where that is all the text gives. Keep the whole phrase together, INCLUDING the unit and any word or letter that names a dimension -- (W) / (H) / (D) / (L), 'wide', 'high', 'deep', 'long' -- and keep them in the order the text writes them; code splits the phrase into width, height and depth and reads those labels. A row giving only ONE dimension must keep its word too (a grille that is only '250 mm high' is a height, not a width). It is NOT the neck size and NOT a diameter -- those have their own attributes.

attribute_definitions.label: Diameter (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: The item's diameter as written. On a ROUND item the neck size IS the diameter, however the row words it, so a round item's stated neck belongs here.

attribute_definitions.label: UL listed
attribute_definitions.note: Owner default (R14) when 'None': non-UL.

attribute_definitions.label: Control panel ratio or outgoing feeder count (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: Owner ruling 5 (2026-09-23): a feeder count ('maximum 6 outgoing feeders') maps to the 1:N panel in code.

attribute_definitions.label: Sheet / panel / plenum thickness or gauge (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: The item's own sheet metal thickness or gauge, NOT an insulation thickness.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulation thickness (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: Owner design fix (2026-09-23): the insulation's thickness, separate from the sheet thickness.

attribute_definitions.label: Area band (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: Owner ruling 6c (2026-09-23): a stated area band such as 'up to 0.5 sqm' or '1.1 to 2.0 sqm'; code takes its maximum and multiplies the per-sq.m rate by it (slice 5).

attribute_definitions.label: Variant
attribute_definitions.note: A CLOSED per-family pick (owner design fix, 2026-09-23) so the sheet's ladder survives. Owner defaults (R14) when 'None': VCD GI rectangular, fire damper without sleeve. A VCD is 'aluminium' ONLY where the row or its headings say the damper is aluminium (aluminium, aluminum, Al.) (owner 2026-10-23); a VCD that does not say aluminium is answered as before and takes the default. A motorised aluminium VCD is 'motorised'.

attribute_definitions.label: How many of this item make ONE unit of the row
Item as written
attribute_definitions.note: When the family is 'none of these', the item the row buys, in the BoQ's own words (one continuous piece, the shortest that names it: 'Hit & Miss Damper', 'Bird Screens with GI wire mesh'). Leave it out for every other family.

hvac_insulation.notes: SLICE 12a (owner I-1): the CATALOGUE and the MECHANISM. Pricing, extraction and the panel are 12b, which is why `pipelines` is empty -- `config_is_eligible` needs pipelines AND definitions, so no BoQ screen changes. The cost parts are stored SEPARATELY and never baked (owner I-3: a row's own parts stay editable); an unclad row stores cost_cladding 0 explicitly. 24G is the same rate as 26G (owner I-10) and differs only in the gauge. SLICE 12c: the pricing RULES, in `list_spec` only -- `pipelines` stays EMPTY so the category is still not eligible and every Insulation BoQ row keeps its coming-soon card (Q13). Cladding is computed from the seven HVAC Pricing Inputs, so `cost_cladding` is no longer stored on the pipe rows. SLICE 12c FINISH: the five CLADDING-ONLY SKUs (owner F1) -- one per cladding type, priced from the ROW'S own pipe size and thickness by the composites' own cladding formula, wastage included. A per-sq.m cladding-only row takes the plain sheet rate with NO overlap (owner F2). FA7 (owner ruling 2026-10-04, option A): `calculator_only` admits this category to the Pricing CALCULATOR tab only -- BoQ rows still show the coming-soon card and the category stays out of the extraction population. TEMPORARY: the slice that makes Insulation fully eligible REMOVES this key in the same slice, so there is never a second on/off switch. Owner 2026-10-04: every attribute is a DROPDOWN built from the active catalogue rows (`panel_controls`), so adding a catalogue item adds its option with no code change. Owner C-R1/C-R2/C-R3 2026-10-04: the pipe size resolves FIRST so a composition is built from ONE pipe size's rows, and a tie that closeness cannot break goes to the lowest summed cost_insulation. SLICE 12d-1a (owner R1-R9, 2026-10-07): the model's questions (item note, 'none of these', the cladding note, brand), the cladding default, family_when_none, value_map, panel_readonly, second_opinion ON while building. calculator_only STAYS; eligibility is 12d-2's. SLICE 12d-1b (owner T1-T8, 2026-10-07): the thickness note (schedule / list / layers as written), numbers.thickness_mm.several = highest, number_defaults.thickness_mm on every family, material_as_written + no_sku_named_by. calculator_only STAYS; eligibility is 12d-2's. SLICE 12d-2 (owner S1-S8, 2026-10-07): SWITCHED ON. `calculator_only` REMOVED -- the category is eligible through the ONE generic predicate (pricing rules that run: its `list_spec.pricing` families; `pipelines` stays EMPTY because every unit block carries its own and a top-level entry would never execute). Insulation rows now price on BoQs and join the extraction population. The thickness note states the four-step read order (S3: the row's OWN value wins; else the heading schedule for THIS row's size; else the list as written; else left out -- the highest / the 9 mm default are CODE, never the prompt). second_opinion stays ON for the paid sample (S8; it goes OFF in 12d-4). SLICE 12d-2F (owner F3, 2026-10-07): the cladding note states that a 22G / 26G GSS perforated sheet on a GI frame IS 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet' (the second opinion had flagged three such rows as 'GSS, not aluminium'); no pricing rule, no item and no other config changed. The FG + GI framework double count fixed in the same slice was a SERVING defect (the read-time cladding projection written into the served rates), not an asset change. SLICE 12d-4a (owner D1-D14 on the 12d-3 audit, 2026-10-11): FOUR new SKUs -- Acoustic Nitrile Insulation x 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet' at 9 / 13 / 15 / 19 mm (cost_insulation derived from the No-cladding row, cost_cladding 0 because the framework is priced live by the pipeline's gi*gif + gia branch, install cladding 150 as the Fiberglass GI rows carry it; source rows numbered past the workbook's last Insulation row -- asset-minted, not workbook rows). FOUR pricing keys: named_in_row (D3: a cladding named in the row's OWN text but answered 'None' refuses for a person; headings never trigger it), unstocked_materials (D7: EPDM and the listed materials refuse by name whatever family the model picked), refuse_on_unit_class (D9b: glass cloth on a sheet row refuses), read_notes (D8: the 'BoQ says 32 kg/m3 -> priced as the 48 kg/m3 board' line). Notes: D5 ('A mm + B mm thick' under a pipe heading is pipe + thickness), D8 (fibre glass of any density is the 48 kg board), D9a (paint over glass cloth is 'Glass Cloth with paint'; aluminium beside it at the stated gauge; no gauge -> 26G), D13 (a bolted-on perforated GSS sheet with no frame is the GI framework cladding). D10 (QRO) and D11 (refusal order) are code. D2 / D6 / D12 / D14: no change by ruling. SLICE 12d-4aF (owner, 'agree. we need to fix'): refuse_on_unit_class now NAMES its families -- Thermal Nitrile, Acoustic Nitrile and the Fiberglass board (the sheet families); Cladding Only per sq.m with glass cloth prices again at the plain rate (12c F2, 294 / 70). Nothing else changed from the 12d-4a asset (the version lives only in the filename). SLICE 12d-4c (owner C1 'agreed', C2 'it is ok. make it explicit', C4 'switch off now'): the item note says a row describing only a cladding or coating over insulation, with no insulation material supplied, is 'Cladding Only'; the cladding note says a bare 'glass cloth' with no paint or coating named is still 'Glass Cloth with paint'; the second opinion is OFF for Insulation (a build-time instrument, switched off before the category goes live -- ADP's stays as it is). attribute_definitions.label: Insulation material
attribute_definitions.note: Which insulation the row buys. The family: it decides the SKU set and the unit. Open cell is Acoustic Nitrile Insulation; closed cell on a duct, sheet, wall, ceiling or slab is Thermal Nitrile Insulation, also where the row or its heading calls it acoustic insulation ('acoustic insulation ... with closed cell nitrile rubber' on a duct is Thermal Nitrile Insulation); closed cell on a pipe is Nitrile Rubber Insulation. Fibre glass, glass wool or resin-bonded glass wool of ANY density -- 32 kg/m3 included -- is ' Fiberglass Rigid Board Insulation, Density 48Kg/m3' (the density is ignored). 'none of these' for an insulation material the catalogue does not stock (rockwool, mineral wool, XLPE, phenolic, EPDM, PIR, polyethylene / EPS). A row that names only a GENERIC insulation -- 'insulation', 'insulation foam', 'foam insulation' -- and no material of its own takes the material its heading names: under a heading naming nitrile rubber it is nitrile (Nitrile Rubber Insulation on a pipe, Thermal Nitrile Insulation on a duct or sheet). 'none of these' is only for a material the catalogue does not stock, never for a generic word. Answer 'none of these' only for a material the BoQ NAMES that the catalogue does not stock; when the row and its headings name no insulation material at all, leave this out -- the pricer applies the ruled default. Where the BoQ offers materials as alternatives ('nitrile rubber/XLPE', 'rockwool/glasswool'), copy the material as written in full, both names, into 'Insulation material as written'. A row that describes only a cladding or coating applied over insulation, with no insulation material being supplied, is 'Cladding Only'. Tubular nitrile rubber, nitrile tube or nitrile tubing (any spelling of nitrile) is Nitrile Rubber Insulation; 'Tubular Puf Insulation' only where PUF or polyurethane is named.

attribute_definitions.label: Cladding
values: GI Framework with perforated Al sheet
attribute_definitions.note: What covers the insulation. 'No' means the row states none. A cladding a heading names applies to every row under it that changes only the material or the thickness and names no cladding of its own: answer the heading's cladding there. A cladding a heading names with 'where required', 'if required', 'as required' or 'as directed' still applies to every row under that heading: answer it. Only a condition that names WHERE the item is (pipes exposed to sun or atmosphere, outdoor, exposed areas) limits the cladding to rows that meet that condition. 'Exposed insulation material with <a cladding>' describes the insulation's own outer face, not a place: that cladding applies to every row under the heading (owner 2026-10-23). Aluminium foil and glass cloth offered as alternatives ('Al Foil / GC cloth') is 'Aluminium Foil'. When neither the row nor its headings mention a cladding, answer 'None' - never leave it out for that reason. 'Al. foil', 'Alu foil' or aluminium foil is 'Aluminium Foil'. A GI or galvanised sheet cladding with no frame and no perforated sheet named ('26 G GI cladding') is not stocked: LEAVE THIS OUT and copy the cladding exactly as written into 'Cladding as written'. A GI frame, grid or framework of any gauge (a 22G GI frame work) carrying a perforated sheet is 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet'. A perforated GSS sheet (galvanised steel sheet, 22G / 26G, powder coated or not) carried on such a frame is the SAME cladding, 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet' -- the sheet metal the row names does not make it a different cladding, so do not flag or withhold it for saying GSS rather than aluminium. A paint or coating over glass cloth (two coats of UV paint, a flame-retardant coating sandwiched with glass cloth) is 'Glass Cloth with paint' -- a paint or coating alone NEVER makes it aluminium. A paint or coating ('polyshield coating', 'fire retardant coating', 'protective coating', a UV coating, a lacquer) is not a cladding and never changes the price (owner 2026-10-23): where it is the only covering the text names, with no glass cloth, answer 'None' -- never 'Glass Cloth with paint' -- and leave it out of 'Cladding as written'. A cladding named beside it (an aluminium sheet, a foil) is answered as that cladding. Where the coating IS sandwiched with or applied over glass cloth, it is the paint of 'Glass Cloth with paint': copy the words up to and including the glass cloth into 'Cladding as written'. A co-extruded polymer jacket or covering is copied as written into 'Cladding as written' and never mapped to a stocked cladding. Where aluminium is ALSO named beside the glass cloth it is '<gauge> Aluminium with Glass Cloth' at the gauge the BoQ states; aluminium named with no gauge is 26G ('26G Aluminium', '26G Aluminium with Glass Cloth'): no gauge stated -> priced as 26G. A perforated GSS sheet bolted or screwed on with no frame named is still 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet'. A bare 'glass cloth' with no paint or coating named is still 'Glass Cloth with paint'. A factory-laminated or reinforced glass cloth or fibre cloth facing ('factory laminated fire resistant fibre cloth fabric', 'reinforced glass cloth') IS the glass cloth cladding: 'Glass Cloth with paint', or '<gauge> Aluminium with Glass Cloth' where aluminium is also named. A FOIL facing ('reinforced foil facing', 'foil facing', 'foil-faced', 'FSK') is 'Aluminium Foil', never a glass cloth (owner 2026-10-23); an aluminium cladding and a foil facing offered as alternatives ('aluminum cladding / reinforced foil facing') is 'Aluminium Foil'.

attribute_definitions.label: Cladding as written
attribute_definitions.note: The cladding in the BoQ's OWN WORDS, copied exactly as the row or its heading writes it ('26 G GI cladding', '24 G aluminium with glass cloth'). Answer it whenever the text names a cladding, also when 'Cladding' is answered; leave it out when no cladding is named. Recorded and shown; the pricer maps a cladding the catalogue does not stock. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Thickness (mm)
attribute_definitions.note: The insulation thickness AS THE ROW WRITES IT, in mm. Never converted. Read it in this order and stop at the first that applies: (1) the row's OWN value -- a thickness in the row's description or in a note attached to the row -- always wins, even where a heading says otherwise; (2) else, where a heading keys the thickness to the pipe size (a schedule such as '25mm to 50 mm : 19mm thick'), read the thickness for THIS row's pipe size and return that one value; (3) else, where the text lists several thicknesses with no such schedule, copy the list as written; (4) else leave the attribute out. Where the text states two layers ('19 mm x 2', '2 layers of 19 mm', '25 mm thick - 2 Layers'), copy it as written -- never add the layers up. Under a PIPE heading, 'A mm + B mm thick' is the PIPE SIZE and the insulation THICKNESS (65 mm + 32 mm thick = a 65 mm pipe with 32 mm of insulation), not two layers: return B here and A as the pipe size. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe size (mm)
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's nominal size AS THE ROW WRITES IT. Pipe families only. Under a pipe heading, 'A mm + B mm thick' names the pipe size first: A is the pipe size, B the insulation thickness. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Brand
attribute_definitions.note: The make or brand the row names for this item, copied as written. It is recorded and shown; it is never used to choose a catalogue row. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulation material as written
attribute_definitions.note: The insulation material exactly as the row or its heading names it (XLPE, rockwool, nitrile rubber). A co-extruded polymer jacket or covering is copied here as written too. Copied as written; it is what a pricer is told when the catalogue has no SKU for it. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Coating as written
attribute_definitions.note: A paint or coating the row or its heading names that is NOT the paint of 'Glass Cloth with paint' (a UV coating, a fire or flame retardant coating, a polyshield or protective coating, a lacquer), in the BoQ's own words; leave it out when no such coating is named. Shown on the panel only: the price never reads it. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe type
attribute_definitions.note: Which pipe THIS row buys - one of the four stocked types. Answer it only when the row's own text, or a heading that describes this row's pipe, names that very type or the service that decides it: copper, refrigerant, VRF or VRV piping is Copper, also where the word copper is not written, and on EVERY pipe row under such a heading, whatever level the heading sits at (a 'VRF SYSTEM' heading two or three levels up still makes each pipe row below it Copper) - unless the row itself, or a nearer heading, names another type for that pipe (a uPVC drain under a VRF heading is uPVC); MS or mild steel piping is MS, and chilled water piping that names no type is MS; PVC is PVC; CPVC is CPVC. A drain or condensate line takes the type the text names for it. A drain pipe whose material the BoQ does not name: leave the pipe type out (do not guess); the code prices it as CPVC. The row's own word wins over a heading: a row that says PVC under a CPVC heading is PVC. Where the text names any other type (GI, uPVC, HDPE, SS, anything else), or names two different types for this pipe and the row itself does not say which, LEAVE THIS OUT - never choose the nearest stocked type; the pricer does that from 'Pipe type as written'. Return one item per pipe the row pays for. Testing, painting, sleeves, welding, nitrogen or vacuum work, civil work, identification and valves named with the pipe are NOT items and change no attribute: ignore them.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe type as written
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's type in the BoQ's OWN WORD, copied exactly as written: from the row's own text when it names one, else from the nearest heading that describes this row's pipe (copper, MS, GI, uPVC, HDPE, SS). Answer it on every pipe whose type the text names, also when 'Pipe type' is answered. Where the text names two or more types for this pipe, copy them all as written ('MS / GI', 'uPVC/ CPVC'). Copy the TYPE word when the row or any heading writes one: under 'COPPER REFRIGERANT PIPINGS' it is 'COPPER', never 'Refrigerant'. Only where no type word is written anywhere in the text, write the service word as written ('VRF', 'refrigerant', 'chilled water') or leave this out. Copy only words the text actually writes - never a type the text does not contain. Leave it out when neither the row nor its headings name a type. Recorded and shown; the pricer maps it or refuses it by name. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe size
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's own size AS THE ROW WRITES IT, with its unit: mm, an NB number (50 NB), inches (5/8", 1-1/4", 2 inch) or an outside diameter in mm (22.3 mm O.D). Never converted, never rounded. The row's own size comes first; a heading gives the size only when the row states none. Where the text names two sizes and says which one is this pipe's, return that one; otherwise copy both as written (25/32 mm). Where the row writes its size as a bare number with no unit (3/4, 1, 1-1/4), take the UNIT - never the size - from a heading that describes this row's pipe, or from the neighbouring rows of the same list (rows beside it written 3/4", 1", 1-1/4" make a bare 1 an inch size), and write the unit with the size ('1 inch'). Where neither the row, its headings nor its neighbours give a unit, return the number bare, exactly as written. A wall thickness, a gauge, a class, a schedule or a pressure rating is NEVER the pipe size: in '22.3 mm O.D (wall Thickness-1.0 mm)' the size is 22.3 mm. A number or a slash pair written next to 'insulation', 'insulated', 'thick' or 'thickness' ('insulation : 13/19 mm', 'with 6/9 mm nitrile rubber insulation', '9 MM insulation foam') is a THICKNESS and is never the pipe size. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Class / wall thickness
attribute_definitions.note: A class, wall thickness, schedule, grade or 'seamless' / 'ERW' the text states for the pipe, copied as written. A wall thickness written beside the size ('100NB - 5.4mm thick (Min)', 'wall Thickness-1.0 mm') is the PIPE's wall thickness: it goes here and is never an insulation thickness. Recorded and shown; it never changes the price (the sheet has one rate per size). Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulated
attribute_definitions.note: Whether THIS pipe is insulated. Yes when the row, or a heading that describes this row's pipe, says it is insulated or gives any insulation fact for it (a material, a thickness, 'duly insulated', 'with 9 MM insulation foam'). No only when the text says this pipe is NOT insulated (bare, uninsulated). Leave it out when the text does not mention insulation for this pipe. When Yes, also return the insulation as its own item in the insulation section, in the same position as its pipe.

Plus the four Misc items VRF takes over now as the SHARED kind hvac_misc_item, each with its Misc-sheet markups -- the future Misc category lists the same stored set, never a copy (R-MISC). DATA-ONLY: no pricing block, so it never prices a BoQ row and the calculator shows 'coming soon' until VRF-2 / VRF-4. The two conversion factors are Pricing Inputs (vrf_hp_per_tr, vrf_kw_per_tr). VRF-2a (owner, 2026-11-03): the VRF families PRICE IN THE CALCULATOR -- the list_spec pricing block below -- while `calculator_only` (owner Q1 A, temporary, removed at VRF-4) keeps every VRF BoQ row on the coming-soon text and every VRF row out of Suggest. The Blue Star ductables VFM-216A (18 TR) and VFM-264A (22 TR) are retired (R-RETIRE): a ductable above 8 TR refuses. The four Misc items stay unpriced until VRF-2c. VRF-2b (owner, 2026-11-03): a capacity stated in HP, TR or kW is read and converted to the family's own unit through the two VRF Pricing Inputs (an airflow refuses, named); the unit picker beside the typed box; the size options show their unit; the four Misc items price here (Nos / Kg, `extra_kinds`); several or off-sheet brands price as Blue Star, naming the row's words; 'Nos/Ro' reads as Nos with a line. calculator_only stays until VRF-4. VRF-3a (owner, 2026-11-04): an Outdoor Unit above the largest size of its brand and variant is split by the helper into separate lines (the fewest units, adding up exactly, else the smallest total above, then the cheapest; each line the row's brand and variant; an edit never re-splits); a split the row writes is one line per module (a module above the largest refuses); a condition the row states is quoted; an airflow range is one airflow; 'Set' prices one piece per Set with a bar (a refnet's pieces come from the system's unit counts); Lot, LS, Job, per HP and 'complete system' refuse with a bar. calculator_only stays until VRF-4. VRF-3b (owner, 2026-11-05): a unit's price can include its copper (Piping), insulation (Insulation) and power / communication cable (Electrical, read only), each its own line per Nos under each indoor / outdoor unit, sized from the Pricing Inputs by the unit's capacity, removable, held when a size is missing; Lot is offered in the calculator's Row unit. calculator_only stays until VRF-4. VRF-4 (owner, 2026-11-06): VRF is live on BoQ rows (calculator_only removed). The model is asked per item whether the unit's price includes copper, insulation, power and communication cable, and copies the sizes, brand, working + standby words and refnet coverage as written; each borrowed field is priced by its own sheet's rules; refnet unit counts are added up from the sheet; a working + standby row prices one unit under a red bar. second_opinion is ON for testing and must be switched off before deploy. VRF-5 (owner, 2026-11-06): an accessory the BoQ says a unit's price includes (MS frame, gas charge, drain pump, remote, refnet, MCCB / isolator) is priced as the unit's own line -- the quantity from the BoQ, else the Pricing Inputs default -- and never blocks the unit; an inclusion only a heading or note states is added unless the same sheet quotes it on its own row, with a review note; a cable named without a size takes the default; an outdoor unit below the smallest Top unit defaults to Side; several makes -> Blue Star if stated, else the first stocked; supply only / installation only (the installation-only uplift is a Pricing Input). second_opinion stays ON for testing and must be switched off before deploy. VRF-6 (owner, 2026-11-09): the remote's type follows the BoQ (ambiguous 'corded or cordless' -> Cordless, then the model's answer, then the words); every included extra that is not added says why; the own-row check reads each row's category first; '12HP x 2NOS' is a written split, a written module above the largest unit is split, a size no single unit matches takes the single that covers it unless a covering pair is cheaper (then the cheaper pair with the least excess); a cable length reaches only its own cable, 'AL' is aluminium, drain-pump cabling is not the power cable; accessories take the unit's make; per outdoor module: one MS frame / stand (its own Nos item), gas kg = HP, one MCB + ELCB by the HP schedule; built-in drain pump, scope conflicts and installation-only settled by the sheet's own rows; control wiring = comm cable; a 'quantified separately' note wins; two capacities refuse. second_opinion is OFF (owner 2026-11-09 18:52: the standing rule for every category, new-category testing included).

'Touch Screen Central Controller' is a central / i-Touch / touch-panel controller for the whole system; 'BACnet Integration Controller for VRF Units' only when the row names BACnet or a BMS gateway. A drain pump bought on its own row is 'Drain Pump'. 'None' when the row does not say what kind of unit it is (an indoor unit whose type is not stated - a person picks it); 'none of these' when the row names an item that is not listed. VRF-5: an accessory the BoQ says is part of a unit's price (frame / stand, gas charge, drain pump, remote, refnet / Y-joint, MCCB / isolator, AV pads and the like) is answered on the unit item (its includes_* questions), never listed as a separate item, unless the row itself is that item. A central controller described as BACnet / BMS compatible is the 'Touch Screen Central Controller' (the BACnet item only when the row itself is a BACnet integration item). A ducted / ceiling suspended ducted indoor unit is 'Ductable'. An inclusion stated in a heading applies to every unit row under it. VRF-6: a frame / stand quoted per Nos is 'MS frame / stand for ODU' (per Kg it stays 'MS Angle Base Frame Structure'). A cassette the BoQ sizes as 600 x 600 mm or 2' x 2' is a Cassette (its way FOUR-WAY COMPACT). A CSU / ceiling suspended unit is 'Ductable'. Cabling the BoQ ties to a drain pump (a plug top, a power point for the pump) is the pump's, not the unit's power cable. VRF-9 (S9 / S10): a row that only charges / tops up refrigerant gas is 'Refrigerant Gas Filling (R-410)'; a row for the outdoor units' MS base frame / stand / structure is 'MS frame / stand for ODU' -- never leave the item out.

Cabling for a drain pump (a plug top, a power point for the pump) is NOT the unit's power cable. VRF-8: REQUIRED on every item - never leave it out. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. With Yes, the _words answer copies ONE exact clause of the BoQ (never '...') and _where says where it sits. 'Necessary interconnections with power supply / earthing / refrigerant connections' is connection work only: No.

A sentence about how the system must behave when the control wiring fails or breaks down is NOT scope. A heading or note at any level that puts the control wiring in the scope IS scope. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. With Yes, the _words answer copies ONE exact clause of the BoQ (never '...') and _where says where it sits. attribute_definitions.label: Valve type
attribute_definitions.note: Which valve or valve-type item THIS row buys. Butterfly Valve = a manual (lever / gear) butterfly valve; Motorised Butterfly Valve = a butterfly valve with an electric / motorised actuator; Balancing Valve = a balancing valve, DRV, double regulating or commissioning set; NRV / Check Valve = any non-return, check or reflux valve; PIBCV = a pressure independent (balancing) control valve, PICV or PIBCV; Sluice / Gate Valve = a sluice or gate valve; Strainer = any strainer; Ball Valve = a ball valve, and a drain valve or drain cock; Test & Drain Valve = only where the row says 'test and drain' valve; Foot Valve = a foot valve; Automatic Air Vent = an automatic air vent / air release / air purger; BTU Meter = a BTU, heat or thermal energy meter; 2-Way Valve = a 2-way (motorised) control valve that is not pressure independent. A thermometer, temperature or pressure gauge, test plug / point, thermowell, rubber bellows, flexible connection or expansion joint is NOT a valve: return it as its own item in the misc section. Answer 'none of these' for any other valve or instrument (a flow meter, a 3-way valve, a pot strainer, a gauge cock, an isolation valve with no type, a valve whose type is not written) and copy its words into 'Valve type as written'. Return one item per valve or instrument the row pays for: a valve named with gauges, a thermometer or another valve is several items. A part built into the valve (its actuator, its flanges, its handle) is never a second item. The row's own text wins over a heading; take the type from a heading only when it describes this row's item (a size-only row under 'Butterfly valves'). A thermostat, controller, remote controller, actuator or actuator panel named WITH a PIBCV (pressure independent control valve) is PART of the PIBCV item - our PIBCV item already includes its thermostat and actuator: return the one PIBCV item and no second item for them. This is only for a PIBCV: a thermostat named with any other valve (a 2-way valve) is still its own item. A ball, gate or needle valve the row ties to a pressure gauge ('for isolation', 'of suitable size', 'cost included in this item', 'with syphon') is part of the gauge: return the gauge alone, in the misc section, and no valve item; a valve the row prices as its own item with its own size stays a separate valve. An automatic air vent with a ball valve: the row's one size is the BALL VALVE's size - put it on the ball valve (the air vent has one price for any size). An abbreviated 'BV' or 'Bal valve' is a Ball Valve when its size is 40 mm or below; above 40 mm take the type from the heading. A valve 'with strainer', or with an integral / built-in strainer, is TWO items: the valve and a Strainer of the same size. A Set whose heading spells out what one Set holds (e.g. one ball valve with strainer and one without) is each of those items, one item each. A kit or package naming several parts: return each part as its own item, so only a part we do not stock is 'none of these'. A ball valve the row ties to a strainer's drain ('ball valve for strainer drain', 'drain valve ... included') is PART of the strainer: return the one Strainer item and no ball valve item; a valve the row prices with its own size stays its own item. A valve that is BOTH balancing and modulating ('2 way modulating balancing valve') is a PIBCV. A 'high rangeability control valve' is a 2-Way Valve with operation Modulating. Under a heading saying 'with and without strainer' over rows that state only a size, return the valve alone (no Strainer item): the BoQ does not say how many have one. A 'swing check' NRV is an NRV / Check Valve: copy 'swing check' in valve_type_as_written and leave nrv_type 'None' (swing check is neither Flanged nor Dual Plate). A balancing valve with INTEGRATED P/T test points is one Balancing Valve item (the test points are part of it); list test plugs only when the BoQ counts separate test points. A '2 way pressure independent on-off' valve is a PIBCV; copy 'on-off' in valve_type_as_written. An air vent named only in the heading, over a row whose own words describe only a ball valve, is not an item: return the ball valve alone.

attribute_definitions.label: Valve type as written
attribute_definitions.note: The valve or instrument's type in the BoQ's OWN WORDS, from the row, else from the nearest heading that describes this row's item. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value. For a kit or package, copy each part's own words on its own item, never the whole package on one item. When the row writes a count for an item ('two', '2 nos', 'pair of'), copy the count with the item's own words. When the row says 'with out valve', copy those words.

attribute_definitions.label: Valve size
attribute_definitions.note: The valve's own size AS THE ROW WRITES IT, with its unit: mm, an NB number (50 NB), DN 50, inches (1-1/2", 2 inch). Never converted, never rounded. A dial size of a gauge or thermometer, a pressure rating (PN 16), a pipe schedule or an insulation thickness is NEVER the valve size. Where the row names two sizes for this item copy both as written (25/32 mm). Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value. A size written in mm with a stray inch mark after it ('15mm"') is that many mm (15 mm), never inches. When the row's own words state a size and the appended heading / description text states another, the row's own size wins (the row's own words come before the first ' | ').

attribute_definitions.label: Actuator duty
attribute_definitions.note: Motorised butterfly valves only: On-Off or Modulating, as the row or a heading describing this valve states. 'None' when not stated. Clear modulating-control wording counts as Modulating even without the word: '4-20 mA', 'analog' / 'analogue' (signal, output, control), 'proportional'.

attribute_definitions.label: 2-way operation
attribute_definitions.note: 2-way valves only: On-Off or Modulating as stated. 'None' when not stated. Clear modulating-control wording counts as Modulating even without the word: '4-20 mA', 'analog' / 'analogue' (signal, output, control), 'proportional'.

attribute_definitions.label: NRV type
attribute_definitions.note: NRV / check valves only: Dual Plate, Ball Type, Wafer, or Flanged (a swing / flanged NRV). 'None' when the row names no NRV type; flanges named only as companion flanges are not a type. A type stated in the row or in a heading describing this valve is read and wins: 'wafer type dual plate check valve(s) ... with companion flanges' is Dual Plate.

attribute_definitions.label: Spindle
attribute_definitions.note: Sluice / gate valves only: Rising or Non-rising spindle as stated. 'None' when not stated.

attribute_definitions.label: Strainer type
attribute_definitions.note: Strainers only: Y-Type or T-Type as stated. 'None' when not stated (a pot / basket strainer is 'none of these' in Valve type).

attribute_definitions.label: Flanged
attribute_definitions.note: Yes when the row, or a heading describing this valve, says the valve is flanged or comes with companion / matching flanges. 'None' when not mentioned.

attribute_definitions.label: Operator as written
attribute_definitions.note: Butterfly valves: the operator the BoQ names (lever, hand lever, gear, gear box, worm gear), copied as written. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Quantity in one row unit
attribute_definitions.note: How many of THIS item make one unit of the row, only where the row states a count for this item ('with 2 nos pressure gauges' -> 2 on the gauge item). 'None' otherwise. Never the row's own quantity, a size or a dial size.

attribute_definitions.label: Scope
attribute_definitions.note: What the row pays for, from its own words first, then a heading describing it: supply + installation (SITC, supply & install, fixing ...), supply only, or installation only. 'None' when nothing is said. 'portable' or 'handed over' means Supply only. 'Supply of ...' and 'Supply and provisioning / providing ...' are Supply + installation (installation is included unless the BoQ says supply only or quotes installation on its own row) - answer the same way on every row with the same wording. Installation (installing, fixing, refixing) of items the row does not supply is Installation only - also refixing, reinstalling, shifting or relocating EXISTING or OLD valves. 'Lifting, shifting, positioning at site' in a list of what the price includes is not installation only.
